The sweep failure was in the test runner, not in the feature's code: every one of the 116 files died at startup with `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'config')` / "Vitest failed to find the runner", the signature of a worker whose globals are gone — this suite shares workers between files (`isolate: false` in `vitest.config.mts`), and vitest 5.0.0 read `process` off the global, so one file leaving it replaced takes every file queued behind it down. I moved the suite to vitest 5.0.3 (5.0.2 binds its own `process`) and kept the shared-worker setting with that reason recorded next to it. Repeated full runs then exposed a second, older Windows flake — `test/repo-map-files.test.ts` failing with `EPERM` on a staged-file rename — so `replaceFile` (`src/agent/workspace-files.ts`) now backs off up to 100 ms per attempt over 150 attempts instead of giving up after half a second, keeping the single-step replace.

Six consecutive full `npm test` runs are green (113 passed, 3 skipped) and `npm run typecheck` is clean; "Reviewing and forgetting" is back to tested with the two fixed files and the reason in its note. The rest of the board is untouched.
